Medical Malpractice Insurance is crippling Obstetrics and Gynecology in SA

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Will you be able to find a specialist to deliver you baby in 2017

Summary:
Gynecologists and Obstetricians are paying R650 000 annually for Medical Malpractice Insurance, it’s risen from R87 000 in 2009 to a proposed R850 000 in 2017, an increase of R400 000 in only 2 years. In order to cover these cost Obstetricians would have to do 26 deliveries a month. The SA Society for Obstetricians and Gynecologist did a survey of 370 of its 800 members and 220 of the 370 said they were leaving the profession in 2017.

Women who can afford private deliveries are being forced into State hospitals which are badly under resourced. Evidence of which is that in 2016 the Medical Malpractice claims were 49 Billion rand more than half the total healthcare budget, and the top of the list of claims were for Obstetrics. With the capping of pay outs for lawyers from the Road Accident Fund attorneys are now trawling the hospitals for clients encouraging them to prosecute only charging them if they are successful. MPS reports that some attorneys are going to schools for the disabled encouraging the parents of children with cerebral palsy to sue.


Further information:
The Medical Aids schemes have not increased their birth cover and pay R3400 per delivery and so the burden has been shifted onto the patient who has to cover the additional R10 to R12 000. With the proposed increase of a further R200 000 in 2018, private Obstetricians cannot afford to stay in business.

An urgent meeting with the Minister of Health Aaron Motsoaledi and the MPS the larger Medical Malpractice Insurers have agreed on a moratorium of the increase pegging it at R650 000 for another 6 months while some solution can be reached.

On top of that there has been a freezing of State posts for Obstetricians for the last 4 years, so doctors are facing unemployment within the state facilities but costs are too high for young doctors entering private practice.

The SASOG are challenging the Insurers to motivate why their cover is so high, how many malpractice suits are there against private Gynecologists? The number of medical litigation against private Obstetricians is very small. They are also proposing a capping of claims and mediation between the claimants and the State so that cases do not have to come before the courts. They are trying to get statutory recognition for a Committee of experienced Obstetricians to provide expert opinion to assist judges with these cases.

SASOG is providing better training to specialists in State hospitals, and establishing better protocols for midwives and interns to try and reduce the number of claims. They have also identified colleagues that have had repeated malpractice claims against them to try and support and train them further.

Press Release:


Medical malpractice insurance
Obstetrics is in crisis in South Africa, with doctors paying close to a million rands for Medical malpractice insurance. It’s estimated that, by 2020, there may not be enough obstetricians in private practice because expensive medical indemnity insurance is driving them away from the profession, leaving patients in the hands of an already overburdened state healthcare system. Carte Blanche investigates


Script:


UPsound from Dr Smit “baby’s heart beat is good
Phathiswa “The doctor said my baby is well everything is going well so I can’t wait to have him
John “How important are appointments like today
Phathiswa ”Very important because they actually give you all the attention you don’t have to struggle to make an appointment and it is very easy to come here
Smit “ The bond between a mother an obstetrician is a quite intense bond and it’s an emotional bond and in more affluent communities woman are prepared to pay for that but in our community that is not possible
Script: Phathiswa Venfolo’s third child will be one of the last babies Dr Steyn Smit will ever deliver
Steyn Smit “ I cannot afford to do obstetrics anymore the insurance has been escalating in such an extent there is no way we can afford to practice obstetrics anymore
Script: In 2009 medical indemnity insurance for Obstetricians was R109 000 - in 2017 it’s R850 000 close to 800 % increase and there is every indication that it could go up to R1 million next year.
Links “The enormous financial pressure on obstetrics is a national issue but it is most keenly felt in less affluent areas like here in Worcester where all 4 of the towns obstetricians have decided to shut up shop
John “Was it a difficult decision?
Smit “It was an extremely difficult decision ……I love doing obstetrics it the most positive and exhilarating procedure anyone can do ….and imagine being able to witness that on a continuous basis everyday of your life it’s an amazing job
Link: For most patients childbirth is the most emotional experience of their entire lives it certainly was for me and when you consider how vulnerable the mother and child are in that moment you realise how important the relationship with the Obstetrician and the midwife is, but alarmingly by 2020 there might be no Obstetricians left in private practice
Carla Foxcroft “Happy moment- we have been coming now for almost 6 years now with Dr van Waart and ja we have just grown a relationship with him
Craig Foxcroft ……if we would be in a government hospital for example what’s the chances are that you might not even know the person
Upsound from Birth
Johannes Van Waart “I think it is really very special – you learn to live with the family we see them at the local restaurant, you see the kids playing around , they come to your table
Script: Dr Johannes Van Waart Chair of the South African Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, says we are in a crisis. In order to cover their costs doctors will have to deliver 27 babies a month, currently the average is 13 ( theatre sequence)
Dr van Waart “It was calculated by an independent source that in order to break even the cost of a delivery should be approximately R13 000 and the medical aids are just ignoring us they are giving us 5.6 % and insurance is increasing by 30-50% a year and at some point it does not make sense anymore and we have seen that I think the worst is still to come ( Hospital images- records theatre)
Smit “to make Obstetrics a viable income then you need to charge double or triple the amount that the medical aid is willing to pay”
Script: They recently ran a survey amongst their members and of the 330 that replied 230 said they were leaving the profession if nothing changed.
Script: The highest number of claims against Obstetricians relate to cerebral palsy. Yet 90% of the time this condition is a result of a variety of complex reasons, and only 10% result from oxygen deprivation at birth
Smit “ There is lots of stuff that can happen during the pregnancy that can give you an adverse outcome which is not in the hands of the doctor it is in the hands of nature and the doctors can’t change the course of nature
Link: In the last 50 years the number of caesarean sections performed worldwide has increased 6 fold and yet the number of children born with Cerebral Palsy has stayed the same.
Script: Paediatric Neurologist Professor Izelle Smuts says the public and the legal profession don’t understand the complexity of what causes Cerebral Palsy
John “Have people over simplified the causes of cerebral palsy
Isette “We must remember that the developing brain is an extremely vulnerable organ and small changes even in utero can have an influence on that so it is over simplified
Link: So what exactly has led to this crisis- well many people are saying that because the road accident fund is no longer the cash cow that it once was lawyers are starting to look for alternatives?
Script: Adv Alan Nelson says the medical profession is in crisis with the dramatic spike in medical malpractice claims in the last 5 years
Adv Nelson “The contingency fees act allows lawyers to take on these cases on the basis that they will only charge if they are successful and then they are entitled to either double their normal fee or to 25% of the capital of the claim depending on which is the lesser
Script: So lawyers stand to make large sums when claims are between 30 and 50 million rand. Cases that would never have been considered in the past are now coming to court
Isette “There is always in medicine a chance that there may be a complication- that is the inherent risk of medicine there is a certain chance no matter what you do no matter how you prevent that certain things can happen and that is not because the doctor did anything wrong it’s because of the inherent complications
Dr van Waart “the level of service that we have delivered has not been deteriorating…. but what has happened is that the quantum of the claims and the big big one here is cerebral palsy has really gone up and the reason for that is most probably because care actually improved
Smit “The time duration that the law suit can be done is much longer for an obstetrician its usually 3 years for any medical malpractice but for obstetricians its 21 years so the obstetrician can be sued 21 years after the delivery of the baby
Script: In fact it could be far longer – it is a long time to have a sword hanging over their heads and even once they retire they are not off the hook - claims can even be made against their Estate
Adv Nelson “There is nothing more destructive to a professional man than to be accused of not having practiced and having done your job in accordance with the standards of your calling and whilst these cases are pending these doctors go through absolute hell, absolute hell in fact there are many recorded suicides
Isette “Negligence is where there is really substandard care and sometimes you also have to distinguish that from adverse events due to system errors and it becomes a very important issue to distinguish also in court , complications per se does not mean the doctor did wrong
Dr van Waart “We actually went to our own business the things that we can control are our actions and we have put in a program that is called the better obs program where we help everybody to standardise protocols and that has proved worldwide to be of good worth
Script: Young doctors like Candice Morrison are not entering the profession because of litigation and high insurance fees
Candice “When I qualified there weren’t a lot of posts available in Government those jobs are like hens teeth- once you get one you tend to stay in them until you retire really and that is a bit of a problem for young qualifying gynae’s that there isn’t a junior consulting post where you are still supervised and you can improve your skills because you qualify not having done a lot of surgery and its quite daunting to go into private practice
Upsound
Helen “ I have been coming to Dr Van Waart for 17 years, it’s a personal relationship and he has got your most precious procession in his hands
Script: Helen Wolfaardt nearly lost her first baby when her placenta ruptured, the baby was running out of oxygen and they only survived because there was an Obstetrician available for an emergency Caesar.
Link: “The Department of Health currently has 60 Billion rand under litigation or roughly a third of it’s entire budget of those claims about 65% are against Obstetricians now if the crisis in Obstetrics continues an additional 140 000 patients could pour into the already overburdened public health system
Izette “We are already running at 100% occupation rate in the neonatal units, our beds are almost always full there is daily search for beds
Script: The R60 Billion for malpractice claims comes out of the general health budget
Izette ”So that money comes from specific hospitals so if that money is from our hospital budget it immediately has an impact on availability of medication upgrading of equipment, staff
Script: In an attempt to deal with the crisis the Minister of Health has issued a directive that all medico legal cases have to go through mediation before they can litigate.
Adv Nelson “Instead of having 10 experts on both sides and spending years and years and years deciding these matters, and huge sums of money parties can come to a solution much quicker at a much earlier stage. 90% of matters that are referred to mediation are successfully resolved especially if one bears in mind that the cost of mediation is less than 1% of what litigation costs
Dr van Waart “We want fairness for the patient but what we don’t want is that people shooting off the hip and actually try and target us and try the medical profession because this is a national asset and this is an asset we need to protect
Script: If there isn’t a dramatic shift soon from insurance companies, medical aides and the legal profession there will be many more communities like Worcester with no access to private Obstetrician
John “Do you know you are one of Steins last patients
Phatiswa “He just told me that, I am just very happy that I am the last one.
John You made it just under the wire
Phatiswa I am just very happy

With the capping of pay outs for lawyers from the Road Accident Fund attorneys are now trawling the hospitals for clients encouraging them to prosecute only charging them if they are successful. MPS reports that some attorneys are going to schools for the disabled encouraging the parents of children with cerebral palsy to sue.
metadata.Further information: The Medical Aids schemes have not increased their birth cover and pay R3400 per delivery and so the burden has been shifted onto the patient who has to cover the additional R10 to R12 000. With the proposed increase of a further R200 000 in 2018, private Obstetricians cannot afford to stay in business. An urgent meeting with the Minister of Health Aaron Motsoaledi and the MPS the larger Medical Malpractice Insurers have agreed on a moratorium of the increase pegging it at R650 000 for another 6 months while some solution can be reached. On top of that there has been a freezing of State posts for Obstetricians for the last 4 years, so doctors are facing unemployment within the state facilities but costs are too high for young doctors entering private practice. The SASOG are challenging the Insurers to motivate why their cover is so high, how many malpractice suits are there against private Gynecologists? The number of medical litigation against private Obstetricians is very small. They are also proposing a capping of claims and mediation between the claimants and the State so that cases do not have to come before the courts. They are trying to get statutory recognition for a Committee of experienced Obstetricians to provide expert opinion to assist judges with these cases. SASOG is providing better training to specialists in State hospitals, and establishing better protocols for midwives and interns to try and reduce the number of claims. They have also identified colleagues that have had repeated malpractice claims against them to try and support and train them further.
